note: SAS advisory implementation guidance for a provider hosted on Google Cloud (story MCE-17). Identification only: each service is named so a provider can locate the vendor's own documentation; nothing here evaluates any product or makes any FedRAMP determination about it, and the rule or KSI statement governs. Service names and documentation URLs were captured from the vendor's public documentation on the capture date; the notes are not vendor text. Deleting this file withdraws the platform (THIRD_PARTY_NOTICE.md, section Removing a third party).

family_guidance.CMU: Use FIPS 140 validated cryptographic modules for federal data: Cloud Key Management Service with hardware-backed protection levels where required for keys, TLS 1.2 or higher, and Assured Workloads controls where the provider uses them. Record module certificates and validation numbers; document any exception formally.
family_guidance.IEC: Define incident evaluation and reporting procedures with the FedRAMP Reportable Incident test, the Potential Agency Impact N-rating scale, and the class-specific reporting timeframes. Wire detection (Security Command Center threat findings, Google Security Operations alerts) to an on-call process that can meet the clock.
family_guidance.MAS: Define the Minimum Assessment Scope narrowly and defensibly: identify every information resource that handles federal data or whose compromise would affect it, justify each exclusion, and keep the inventory machine-generated (Cloud Asset Inventory exports) so it stays current.
family_guidance.VDR: Run continuous vulnerability detection across every in-scope resource (Security Command Center vulnerability findings, Artifact Analysis for images and packages, VM Manager patch reporting on Compute Engine), meet the class cadences for sample and drift detection, track mitigation and remediation against the timeframes, and honor CISA KEV due dates.

ksi_guidance.KSI-CED-RAT: Review all training content and completion on a defined cycle; keep the review dated and owned. Where completion records live in a learning system, export them on the same cycle. Evidence: review records with reviewer, date and outcome, plus the updated training register.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CMT-LMC: Log and monitor every modification to the offering: Cloud Audit Logs (Admin Activity and Data Access) routed by Cloud Logging sinks to a log bucket in a separate project, Cloud Asset Inventory feeds for resource changes, Cloud Monitoring alerting on writes made outside the pipeline's service account. Evidence: sink and audit configuration exports, asset feed configuration, alert history.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CMT-RMV: Deploy changes by redeploying version-controlled resources through Infrastructure Manager or Config Connector from the pipeline, not by editing live resources. Evidence: Cloud Deploy or Cloud Build release records diffed against Admin Activity audit log writes; drift reports from the declarative tooling.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CMT-RVP: Review change management procedure effectiveness on a cycle: measure failed changes, rollbacks and out-of-band changes, and adjust the procedure. Evidence: dated reviews with metrics and resulting changes.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CMT-VTD: Automate testing and validation of changes in Cloud Build: pre-deployment tests, policy checks against Organization Policy constraints and Infrastructure Manager plans, Binary Authorization attestations on images, post-deployment verification in Cloud Deploy. Evidence: build and release records showing each gate passed per change.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-DFP: Strictly define functionality and privileges for infrastructure and services: least-privilege Identity and Access Management roles on Google Cloud, Organization Policy constraints at the organization and folder level, Policy Intelligence insights on unused permissions. Evidence: IAM policy exports, constraint inventory, insight findings and their closure.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-EIS: Class-varying (optional/MAY at Class B, required at Class C): automated services persistently assess the security of all machine-based information resources and automatically enforce their intended operational state. On Google Cloud: Security Command Center posture management with Organization Policy constraints, Config Connector reconciling declared resources, VM Manager OS policies on Compute Engine instances. Evidence: posture deployment records, reconciliation logs, OS policy reports over time.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-IBP: Persistently check third-party machine-based resources against the original provider's documented secure-configuration benchmarks: Security Command Center compliance standards and VM Manager OS policy assignments on Google Cloud. Evidence: benchmark finding counts per standard over time.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-MAT: Minimize attack surface and lateral movement: VPC Service Controls perimeters around data services, Organization Policy constraints that restrict public IP addresses and public bucket access, private connectivity to Google Cloud APIs, Cloud Next Generation Firewall policies. Evidence: perimeter configuration, constraint inventory, Security Command Center public-exposure findings trend.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-OFA: Review resources for high availability and rapid recovery: regional and multi-zone deployment on Compute Engine and Google Kubernetes Engine, health checks on load balancers, Backup and DR plans, tested recovery. Evidence: architecture inventory with zone coverage, recovery test records.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-RNT: Limit inbound and outbound network traffic: Cloud Next Generation Firewall policies that deny by default, hierarchical firewall policies at the organization level, Google Cloud Armor on public entry points, egress control through VPC Service Controls. Evidence: firewall policy exports, Security Command Center open-firewall findings, Google Cloud Armor policy coverage.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-RVP: Review protection against denial of service and unwanted activity: Google Cloud Armor policies and adaptive protection on external load balancers, Security Command Center threat findings review. Evidence: protection coverage inventory and dated effectiveness reviews.
ksi_guidance.KSI-CNA-ULN: Use logical networking to enforce traffic flow controls: VPC network segmentation, firewall policies per segment, VPC Service Controls perimeters for service access paths, flow log analysis in Cloud Logging. Evidence: network architecture records, flow log analysis, connectivity test results.
ksi_guidance.KSI-IAM-AAM: Automate the lifecycle and privileges of all accounts, roles and groups: Cloud Identity with automated provisioning and deprovisioning from the identity provider, group-based role grants, Policy Intelligence insights on unused access. Evidence: provisioning logs, access review records, orphan-account checks.
ksi_guidance.KSI-IAM-APM: Use passwordless authentication where feasible (FIDO2 security keys), otherwise phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication enforced in Cloud Identity; eliminate long-lived service account keys through Organization Policy constraints. Evidence: enforcement settings exports, Cloud Audit Logs login analysis, service account key inventory.
ksi_guidance.KSI-IAM-ELP: Ensure each user and device can only access what it needs: periodic access reviews, least-privilege role design, Identity-Aware Proxy context-aware access for administrative interfaces, Policy Intelligence insights on unused permissions. Evidence: access review records, insight findings and their closure.
ksi_guidance.KSI-IAM-JIT: Use a least-privileged, role-based, just-in-time authorization model: Privileged Access Manager entitlements granted with approval and expiry; no standing privileged grants. Evidence: entitlement grant logs with approvals and automatic expiry.
ksi_guidance.KSI-IAM-SNU: Use appropriately secure authentication for non-user accounts and services: workload identities and short-lived credentials on Google Cloud; no user-managed service account keys; rotate any unavoidable secrets in Secret Manager. Evidence: service account key inventory, key-age reports, Secret Manager rotation status.
ksi_guidance.KSI-IAM-SUS: Disable or secure privileged accounts in response to suspicious activity: Security Command Center threat findings wired to automated response (disable service account keys, revoke sessions) with on-call escalation. Evidence: response runbooks plus executed-response records with timestamps.
ksi_guidance.KSI-INR-AAR: Generate after action reports for incidents and incorporate lessons persistently. Evidence: after action reports linked to incidents, with tracked improvement actions and closure.
ksi_guidance.KSI-INR-RIR: Review incident response procedure effectiveness on a cycle, including exercises. Evidence: dated reviews, exercise records, and procedure updates that resulted.
ksi_guidance.KSI-INR-RPI: Review past incidents for patterns and previously missed vulnerabilities. Evidence: periodic pattern-analysis reports referencing the incident register.
ksi_guidance.KSI-MLA-ALA: Class-varying (optional/MAY at Class B, required at Class C): a least-privileged, role/attribute-based, just-in-time authorization model governs access to log data by data sensitivity, and is persistently reviewed. On Google Cloud: log buckets in a dedicated project, Privileged Access Manager for time-bound log access, field-level access restrictions in Cloud Logging. Evidence: IAM policy on the logging project, entitlement grant records, periodic access reviews of the log store.
ksi_guidance.KSI-MLA-EVC: Persistently evaluate and test the configuration of machine-based resources, especially infrastructure as code: policy-as-code in Cloud Build on Infrastructure Manager plans, Security Command Center misconfiguration findings in runtime. Evidence: pipeline policy results per change and finding counts over time.
ksi_guidance.KSI-MLA-LET: Maintain and review a list of resources and event types that will be logged, monitored and audited, and confirm those activities occur: the register mapped to Cloud Logging sinks and Data Access audit log configuration per service. Evidence: the logging register plus sink and audit configuration exports proving each listed source emits.
ksi_guidance.KSI-MLA-OSM: Operate a SIEM or similar for centralized, tamper-resistant logging: Cloud Logging sinks to a log bucket or a Cloud Storage bucket in a separate project with Bucket Lock retention, Google Security Operations or another SIEM for analysis, restricted access. Evidence: sink and retention configuration, lock status, access policies.
ksi_guidance.KSI-MLA-RVL: Persistently review and audit logs: automated detections (Security Command Center, Cloud Monitoring alerting policies, Google Security Operations rules) plus a documented human review cadence for what automation cannot judge. Evidence: detection inventory, alert dispositions, review records.
ksi_guidance.KSI-PIY-GIV: Generate real-time inventories automatically from authoritative sources: Cloud Asset Inventory as the inventory of record, exportable on demand. Evidence: on-demand inventory exports with timestamps proving real-time generation.
ksi_guidance.KSI-PIY-RES: Demonstrate and review executive support for security goals persistently: executive sponsorship in the charter, recurring leadership reviews of posture, funded remediation. Evidence: dated leadership review records and funding decisions tied to security goals.
ksi_guidance.KSI-PIY-RIS: Review the effectiveness of security investments persistently: track spend against measurable outcomes (findings closed, coverage gained) and adjust. Evidence: periodic investment-effectiveness reviews with metrics and resulting decisions.
ksi_guidance.KSI-PIY-RSD: Review the effectiveness of security and privacy in the SDLC against CISA Secure By Design principles: pipeline security gates, secure defaults, threat modeling. Evidence: SDLC review records mapped to Secure By Design principles with improvement actions.
ksi_guidance.KSI-PIY-RVD: Operate and persistently review a vulnerability disclosure program: a public intake channel, triage SLAs, and periodic effectiveness review. Evidence: the published policy, intake and triage records, dated program reviews.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SCR-MIT: Persistently identify, review, and mitigate supply chain risks: supplier vetting, dependency review, risk register entries with mitigations. Evidence: the supply chain risk register with review dates and mitigation status.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SCR-MON: Automatically monitor third-party software for upstream vulnerabilities: Artifact Analysis scanning of images and packages in Artifact Registry, software bill of materials generation in Cloud Build, advisory feeds. Evidence: scan results over time, advisory response records, SBOM currency.
ksi_guidance.KSI-RPL-ABO: Keep backups aligned with defined recovery objectives: Backup and DR plans matching the stated recovery point objective, multi-region copies where the objectives require. Evidence: backup plan configuration, job success history, restore points against objectives.
ksi_guidance.KSI-RPL-ARP: Maintain a recovery plan aligned with objectives, covering roles, procedures, and dependencies. Evidence: the plan with review dates and alignment to the stated RTO and RPO.
ksi_guidance.KSI-RPL-RRO: Define recovery time and recovery point objectives and keep them current. Evidence: documented RTO and RPO with rationale and review history.
ksi_guidance.KSI-RPL-TRC: Test the capability to recover from incidents and contingencies: restore tests from Backup and DR, regional failover exercises, game days, measured against objectives. Evidence: test records with measured times against objectives and corrective actions.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-ACM: Manage configuration with automation and review drift persistently: infrastructure as code as the source of truth through Infrastructure Manager or Config Connector, Security Command Center misconfiguration findings, VM Manager OS policies, automated remediation where safe. Evidence: drift findings and their resolution over time.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-ASM: Automate management, protection, and rotation of keys, certificates, and secrets: Cloud Key Management Service rotation schedules, Certificate Manager and Certificate Authority Service for certificate lifecycle, Secret Manager rotation. Evidence: rotation status across all three, alerts on failures.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-EIS: Persistently evaluate resources for security improvement opportunities and implement them: Security Command Center findings triage, Policy Intelligence insights with tracked adoption. Evidence: findings trend plus a record of improvements shipped.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-PRR: Class-varying (optional/MAY at Class B, required at Class C): plans, procedures, and resource state are persistently reviewed after changes to limit and remove unwanted residual elements that could affect confidentiality, integrity, or availability of federal customer data. On Google Cloud: post-change review of Cloud Asset Inventory diffs for orphaned resources, cleanup through the pipeline. Evidence: post-change review records, residual-resource cleanup logs.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-RUD: Class-varying (optional/MAY at Class B, required at Class C): unwanted federal customer data is removed promptly when an agency requests it per customer agreements, including from backups where appropriate (e.g. data spill or usage change). On Google Cloud: deletion procedures that cover Cloud Storage object versions and Backup and DR restore points, with Sensitive Data Protection scans confirming removal where applicable. Evidence: data-removal request handling records, backup-scoped deletion procedures and logs.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-SIN: Encrypt or otherwise secure information from unwanted access or modification: customer-managed encryption keys in Cloud Key Management Service, TLS 1.2 or higher in transit, Organization Policy constraints that require customer-managed keys and block public access. Evidence: constraint inventory, key usage reports, Security Command Center encryption findings.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-VCM: Class-varying (optional/MAY at Class B, required at Class C): the authenticity and integrity of communications between machine-based information resources is persistently validated using automation. On Google Cloud: mutual TLS through Cloud Service Mesh, workload identities, signed inter-service requests. Evidence: mesh identity validation records, automated integrity-verification records.
ksi_guidance.KSI-SVC-VRI: Use cryptographic methods to validate the integrity of machine-based resources: Binary Authorization attestations on container images, image digests pinned in deployment, Artifact Analysis provenance records, Cloud Audit Logs kept in restricted log buckets. Evidence: attestation and digest verification records in the pipeline.
